object_description: three-layered volume parallel to the slope under a series of three gently sloping pitched roofs
geometry_property: roof arching up over the middle layer
design_condition: the building runs parallel to the slope in the extension of the existing gymnasium wing, defining a protected park and creating three open spaces of independent character across the school site

positive: The building blends into the varied development pattern of the district, running parallel to the slope
Standing in the extension of the existing gymnasium wing it creates a strong spatial relationship to the existing building
The clear definition of the protected park with a ground floor cafeteria gives great potential for a lively neighbourhood park
Three open spaces with an independent character are created across the whole school site
The recessed ground floor creates a spacious covered forecourt along the entire length of the building
This allows attractive views of the park and zenithal lighting of the rear rooms
The covered entrance on the slope side is accompanied on both sides by open atriums
The lateral roof edge traces the three-layer plan in a slightly playful manner
The volumetry of three gently sloping pitched roofs refers to the long narrow row buildings of the quarter
Over the middle layer the roof arches up to bring daylight to the central cluster zone
The sports facilities appear only as a topographical edge and form a plinth that lights the basement rooms from the side
A mixed wood-concrete construction with recycled concrete shell and wooden parapet elements is envisaged
The design was rated positively in terms of the local climate
The volumetric positioning creates two strong, convincing references to the outside space
A mature design whose strengths lie in the clear connection between the two outdoor areas, creating spaciousness
negative: The arrangement generates a relatively large underground footprint
Reducing the above-ground volume reinforces the large-scale development, with a negative impact on costs
The immediate proximity to the listed school building was questioned
The situation created between old and new gymnasium is rather narrow
The distribution of the five clusters across the two stairwells was discussed
The architectural expression of the side facades was discussed
The primary structure and static system of the upper floors lose structural clarity in the basement
The position of the building acts as a barrier to the incoming cold air
The internal organisation was not entirely convincing despite the coherent cluster organisation
